newsitem.title: CHINA: China National Aviation to manage Zhejiang airline.
newsitem.headline: China National Aviation to manage Zhejiang airline.

text.p: China National Aviation Corp (CNAC), the main shareholder of Hong Kong's Dragon Airlines, has taken over operation of eastern China's Zhejiang Airlines, Zhejiang airline officials said on Monday.

China National Aviation had assumed formal control over Zhejiang Airlines from last Sunday after its bid was approved by the Civil Aviation Administration of China (CAAC) earlier this year, a Zhejiang Airlines official said.
The move was intended to improve the state-owned airline's management, which had previously fallen under both CAAC and Zhejiang provincial authorities, the official said.
"The CNAC takeover will be good for the development of the local airline," he said by telephone.
Zhejiang Airlines, based in the Zhejiang capital of Hangzhou, operated five aircraft and had placed orders for three more with Airbus Industrie, another company official said.
"We will take delivery of three Airbus A320 passenger aircraft from Europe, the first to be delivered next year," the official said.

Zhejiang Air operates 14 domestic routes to major cities such as the capital Beijing, Harbin in the northeast, and Guangzhou in the south, he said, adding that the airline had plans to start international routes.
The officials declined to give further details.
